decisions.reason: The source introduces a champagne-gold finish while explicitly preserving the established architectural character; it does not change the Hero V geometry.
The material exploration must preserve the existing architectural feel, but it does not modify the E or L letterform construction or design-language requirements.
Applying champagne gold to the wordmark does not change the second V's optical construction, geometry, locked status, or relationship to the Hero V.
The source changes material and color treatment only and does not alter kerning, spacing, or rhythm.
The champagne-gold treatment does not change the requirement that the É accent reuse the exact Hero V terminal geometry.
The source does not change the second V's scale, prominence, or height relationships within the wordmark.
Material and finish exploration does not alter the exact peak-alignment relationship between the Hero V and É accent.
The new finish does not modify the shared terminal's geometry, intent, refinement constraints, or evaluation rule.
The source does not change the E and L cap-height relationship to the second V.
The material-direction decision does not alter the requirement to include design rationale with review rounds.
The source changes the wordmark's material treatment without changing its common-baseline alignment.
The champagne-gold design direction has no effect on the accepted proof attachment formats.
